newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle heads for early landing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle heads for early landing.

text.p: The space shuttle Columbia began an hour-long descent from space on Tuesday to end its mission curtailed by a malfunctioning power generator.
Mission commander Jim Halsell and pilot Susan Still fired Columbia's twin braking rockets at 1:31 p.m. (1731 GMT) as they orbited high above the Indian Ocean.

Touchdown in breezy conditions at the Kennedy Space Centre was scheduled for 2:33 p.m. EDT (1833 GMT). Flight controllers at mission control in Houston determined the winds would be within the shuttle's safety parameters.

NASA ordered an early end to the planned 16-day science mission because one of the shuttle's three electricity-generating fuel cells was degrading and, in a worst case scenario, could have sparked a fire and an explosion.
The loss of the device should not affect the performance of the $2 billion gliding spaceplane, which can land safely on two working generators.
"Most of our equipment will be running that we require for landing," Still had told a news conference. Some landing systems will be activated later than usual to conserve power, she explained.
It was only the third time in 83 missions that a shuttle had been called home early because of a mechanical breakdown.
The $5 million fuel cell behaved unusually during Columbia's countdown, but appeared to have returned to normal before Friday's blastoff.
Engineers had seen similar pre-launch readings from other fuel cells which later encountered no problems in flight.
One such fuel cell on shuttle Atlantis was being replaced on Tuesday as precaution, NASA spokesman Bruce Buckingham said. Atlantis was scheduled to fly to the Russian space station Mir next month.
Columbia's astronauts shut down their space laboratory earlier on Tuesday, with only a fraction of their $84 million research programme accomplished.
"We're just sorry we're having to close up shop early," mission control's Marrc Garneau radioed the crew.

Scientists have requested another shuttle flight for their space laboratory, which was to have studied the behaviour of fire in space, the growth of plants, the structure of proteins and the manufacture of ultra-pure materials.
